about: What a build of the consumer bundles reads when it runs with no network and no .git, and how to give it what it reads; and, under `firmware`, each firmware build a lane runs, as the cargo command, environment and product that lane builds from. Held by scripts/lib/offline_build.py (--check derives it from the crates graph and the tree, --build builds every bundle in a sandbox that has nothing else, --firmware-cargo / --firmware-env / --firmware-field print a firmware build as its lane reads it); the design is docs/target-build-contract.md section 5d.

source.tree: the files the repository tracks at the commit, without .git

submodules.commit: the gitlink the tree records at this path

commit_input.value: what `git describe --always --dirty=-modified --abbrev=40 --exclude=*` answers in a checkout of the commit: the commit of 40 lowercase hex digits for a clean tree
commit_input.without_it: the build names itself `release` where a checkout build names the commit

cargo.crates: every package of the lockfile, from crates.io, vendored (`cargo vendor --locked`); the lockfile has no git source

cc.what: a C compiler driver and the assembler and linker it runs by name from PATH (gcc's -print-prog-name answers `as` and `ld`); rustc also calls it as the linker

c++.what: a C++17 compiler driver; it runs the assembler `cc` brings

ar.what: an archiver for the static libraries build scripts make

libclang.what: the libclang shared library and its resource headers, which bindgen loads while a build script runs (librocksdb-sys's for the bundles; lwip-sys's for the firmware, which reads the freestanding headers for a -none-eabi target); a library, not a command

arm-none-eabi-gcc.what: the bare-metal ARM C compiler driver, with newlib's C headers, that lwip-sys's build script compiles lwIP with for a -none-eabi target (the cc crate's prefix for it); it runs its own assembler by an absolute path, and the image is linked by the toolchain's rust-lld

arm-none-eabi-ar.what: the archiver the cc crate takes for a -none-eabi target when it answers --version, for lwip-sys's static library

output_variables.note: variables a build script reads that change what it produces; a build identical to a checkout build leaves them unset

firmware.what: the admin node image for QEMU's mps2-an385 with an allocator: the manifest's default feature `heap`, the growable node on embedded-alloc's heap

node_id_source.rendering: the constant's bytes read as one little-endian integer, printed as lowercase hex with no leading zero, as zenoh prints an id (wz_session_core::zid_hex); src/fixed.rs and src/fixed_tcp.rs take the same constant from the crate root

firmware.what: the fixed-memory image of the same node (src/fixed.rs): no allocator, built to the same binary path as the heap image

node_id_source.rendering: the constant's bytes read as one little-endian integer, printed as lowercase hex with no leading zero, as zenoh prints an id (wz_session_core::zid_hex); src/fixed.rs and src/fixed_tcp.rs take the same constant from the crate root

firmware.what: the fixed-memory node with its links on tcp/ (src/fixed_tcp.rs), over the lwIP port that turns TCP on and sizes it; built to the same binary path

node_id_source.rendering: the constant's bytes read as one little-endian integer, printed as lowercase hex with no leading zero, as zenoh prints an id (wz_session_core::zid_hex); src/fixed.rs and src/fixed_tcp.rs take the same constant from the crate root

not_inputs.why: no build script of any bundle reads it: it is what wz's zenoh-c oracle lanes compare the drop-in against
